name: ViewTabBar
intent: Underline-style tab bar for switching between peer views; transparent by default for headers, with an explicit card surface when it must own a filled background.
when: Switch between a few peer views with an underline indicator

chooseOver.because: Tabs bundle content panels; ViewTabBar is just the bar — you render the active view yourself

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a card background to an underline tab bar already placed inside a header
commonMistakes.symptom: The tabs render as a filled strip instead of belonging to the surrounding header
commonMistakes.fix: Keep the default surface="transparent"; request surface="card" only when the tab bar owns a standalone surface.
commonMistakes.avoidOverride: Do not add bg-card around header-integrated ViewTabBar; use its surface prop.

ownership.expectedWrapper: An items-end header row whose single bottom divider belongs to the wrapper. Use surface="card" only when ViewTabBar owns a standalone filled surface.

extracted: cva variants/sizes remain generated by the structural extractor

props.name: surface
props.description: `underline` only — background surface. Use `transparent` in page/route headers and `card` in contained panels.

props.name: fill
props.description: `underline` only — stretch each tab to the full height of the bar's container and vertically center its label. Use inside a fixed-height header row so the tab text lines up with the header's other text while the active underline drops to the container's bottom edge (the shared divider).

props.name: weekSelector
props.description: `segmented` only — a WeekSelector rendered on the right of the toolbar (period navigation). Pass the WeekSelector's props; it renders `bare` by default so it sits flush in the bar (override with `bare`). The view switcher and the period selector are paired frequently, so this variant builds them together.

props.name: trailing
props.description: `segmented` only — extra content on the right of the toolbar (e.g. action buttons).

props.name: labels
props.description: How tab labels show alongside their icon: - `show` (default) — icon + text. - `hide` — icon only; the label moves to a hover tooltip (requires each tab to have an `icon`). - `responsive` — text hides below the `@5xl` container breakpoint (icon only when narrow), with a tooltip standing in. Use inside a `@container` header so it collapses as the header narrows.

props.name: wrap
props.description: `underline` only — let tabs wrap onto multiple lines instead of overflowing (never scrolls).

usage: Use ViewTabBar to help users navigate through your application or content hierarchy. This component provides clear wayfinding and helps users understand their current location within the interface.

ViewTabBar is ideal for multi-page applications, content-heavy interfaces, or any situation where users need to move between different sections. Keep navigation patterns consistent across your application for better user experience.

anatomy.description: ViewTabBar is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Keep tabs concise
bestPractices.description: Use short, descriptive labels for tab triggers.

bestPractices.title: Don't use long tab labels
bestPractices.description: Avoid lengthy text that causes tabs to wrap or overflow.

bestPractices.title: Maintain content relationship
bestPractices.description: Ensure tab content is clearly related to the tab label.

bestPractices.title: Don't use for navigation
bestPractices.description: Use proper navigation components for page-level routing.

bestPractices.title: Show active state clearly
bestPractices.description: Make the selected tab visually distinct from others.

bestPractices.title: Don't hide the active indicator
bestPractices.description: Always show which tab is currently selected.
